chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw a group of people riding behind a coffin, so he said: 'Are these not ashamed of following their companion while riding, when they are delivering him (to the grave) in this state?'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding riding behind a funeral procession?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic etiquette of humility during funeral processions, where the living should walk on foot to show respect to the deceased who is being carried. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted as a sign of modesty (hayā’) and equality before death, contrasting with the pride of riding. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining dignity and reverence in communal mourning rituals.
